title: Crypto misuse: CMAC key not zeroized when HAVE_CMAC_FREE is undefined
description:
wolfssl_cmac_aes_sess_reset and wolfssl_cmac_aes_sess_free call wc_CmacFree only when HAVE_CMAC_FREE is defined (wolfssl_cmac.c lines 124-125 and 152-153).

If wolfCrypt is built without HAVE_CMAC_FREE (which is the case in some wolfCrypt configurations), wc_CmacFree is never called. The Cmac struct stores the AES key material internally (the subkeys K1/K2 derived from the block cipher key, plus the running block state). Without wc_CmacFree, these subkeys are not formally released through the wolfCrypt API.

The ctx-level memzero_explicit(ctx, sizeof(*ctx)) in sess_free does overwrite the embedded Cmac struct, which covers the case for the context struct itself. However, if wc_InitCmac internally allocated heap memory (which some wolfCrypt versions do for certain hardware acceleration paths), those heap allocations will be leaked without wc_CmacFree, and the heap-allocated key material will not be zeroized.

The conditional compile creates silent non-FIPS behavior: on builds where HAVE_CMAC_FREE is not defined, FIPS 140-3 zeroization requirements may not be fully met for heap-allocated internal CMAC state.

Trigger: build with wolfCrypt that does not define HAVE_CMAC_FREE.
Consequence: potential key material leak in heap (implementation-dependent); FIPS 140-3 zeroization may be incomplete.
close_reason: false positive: memzero_explicit(ctx, sizeof(*ctx)) already present unconditionally outside HAVE_CMAC_FREE guard in sess_free; sess_init error path also already correct
